_doc: Lane-plugin delegation — the single source of truth for which dsh plugins mount WHERE, keyed the same way lane routing keys work: platform (the node's OS) and node (glob vs the runner name). Three seams: 'native-web' primes the env of the runner's own proven web-search mount (run-dsh-agent.sh section 2e — per-job copy + regenerated patch overlay); 'plugin' mounts compose-style (in-tree package copied per-job into the profile module tree + insert-row overlay); 'profile-config' turns ON a capability a package already ships but ships OFF — it copies nothing, gates on the package being present in the job's profile module tree, and stamps a bare restating row (patch rows REPLACE whole plugin config, so every shipped field the entry cares about must be restated; entry 'shared_index' swaps the config 'path' for a per-job db file under a shared per-box directory, because the backend owns one process per index path and node:sqlite throws immediately on lock contention). The runner consults this at SPAWN time (scripts/lane-plugins-consult.py) — no node env changes, no node restarts, plugins land by landing this file. External sources are materialized to the per-box canonical location by scripts/sync-lane-plugins.sh from the keepalive (after the v1 checkout), so pins advance on tag bump.
_gates: Every entry gates before mounting: platform must match, node glob must match, and the entry's own gate must pass (require_browser: at least one probed browser exists — probed paths must be space-free for the env pin; probe_port: 127.0.0.1:port must answer — engine-dependent plugins mount only where the engine runs; require_profile_packages: every named package must ship complete in the job's profile module tree; profile-config 'package': same presence check for the restated row's own package). A gated-out entry is a LOUD skip, never a dead mount and never a failed run.
_adoption: Gated like the ADR (2026-08-27): pinned refs, deliberate advancement, smoke before fleet-wide. Manual per-box mounts are the 2026-09-21 incident class — never again.

macos._doc: ctx.web provider 'headless-browser' (issue #293, ADR 2026-08-27). Rode the CI-era cell; the decouple orphaned it — this re-mounts it on every macOS node via the runner's native seam. Canonical source kept by the keepalive sync at ~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@local/dsh-web-search-browser (2e's default path).
macos._browsers_note: Space-free paths only (the env pin validates [A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]); Brave/Chrome .app paths carry spaces and stay to the plugin's internal discovery. chrome-headless-shell is the cell-proven renderer (ADR mount notes).

macos._doc: reflex_* session tools — thin client for the Reflex command server in the Gauge host (one engine, many hosts; TCC grants live in the engine). Mounts only where the engine actually answers.

Standing reflex directive in the lane home's system prompt (issue #254: 0 reflex_ invocations across 1,387 sessions proves steering alone never reaches tower-minted agents; the owner-visible symptom is dialogue pop-ups persisting on the mini display). Merges the managed marker block from config/system-prompts/macos.md into target_file — the ~/.dsh/system-prompt.md global block the dsh-system-prompt-editor reads. Marker-scoped: operator text outside the block is never touched; an unchanged block is a quiet no-op. Gated on the reflex engine port for the same reason the dsh-reflex mount is — a directive naming tools that cannot answer here is a dead prompt. TCC consent dialogs are explicitly EXCLUDED (owner-once, flag in thread).

FLEET session corpus (issue #110's shared location, superseded for claim lanes by the 2026-10-13 purge postmortem ask 1 — FleetTower#2641): the row used to root persistence at ~/.dsh/sessions, so every dispatched job WROTE its workspace into the box's real dsh home — which on a web box IS the user's chat history (194 claim-lane workspaces measured in the user corpus, 2026-10-24). Dispatched jobs now root writes at the fleet-owned corpus under the agent home — the same home the native node's env carries as DSH_SESSIONS_HOME, so node reads, driver probes, and the receipted #2396 prune all name one corpus. The #110 requirement survives: prior-session search sees accumulated history — the fleet corpus accumulates claim history (the tower's one-time migrate-claim-sessions.sh pass seeds it from the user corpus), and the shipped profile row still roots USER web chats at the real home, untouched (user chats never consult this manifest; only the dispatched runner does). ensure_dir makes the consult mint the corpus 0700 before the first job writes there.

Session search backend ON (issue #110): the profile ships this row as path ':memory:' / openAt 'never' — FTS5 search deliberately off. Both shipped fields are restated (patch rows replace whole config). openAt 'first-search' keeps boot unaffected (an unopenable index fails one search, never service activation). 'shared_index' stamps a per-job db under the shared per-box dir: ONE shared file would break the backend's single-process-owner contract — it reconciles under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with no busy timeout, and node:sqlite throws immediately on lock contention, so the worker's parallel slots would flake every search. The index is the backend's own 'dedicated disposable database'; the durable half of sharing is the corpus row above. The index dir moved to the fleet agent home with the corpus row (FleetTower#2641): a dispatched job's search index is derived CLAIM text — it belongs in fleet space, not beside the user's dsh home.

The five model-facing session tools (issue #110): session_search / session_event_search / session_trace / session_event_trace / session_event_read — verify-before-dismissal's native search. Vendored build (plugins/tool-session-query, upstream npm @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-session-query 0.1.0-rc.8 — no dsh release depends on it and the harness git tree has no built lib/, so in-tree is the only self-contained mount; the newer alpha line imports session APIs the deployed rc-era profile tree does not export and fails the live boot proof). Gated on the backend shipping in the profile tree; without it the tools would register and fail every call — a dead mount wearing a working one's clothes.
